Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's…

item.title: Authentication Bypass in CAST Imaging
item.description: CAST Imaging is vulnerable to authentication bypass in the TenantFilter class. The TenantFilter processes the X-ISSUER-LOCATION HTTP header and dynamically registers an OpenID Connect issuer based on its value. An unauthenticated remote attacker can register a malicious identity provider, create users matching existing administrative usernames, and obtain valid JWTs which will be accepted by the application. This…

item.title: ALTCHA PHP: verifySolution bypasses HMAC signature check when challenge signature is absent
item.description: In altcha-org/altcha v2, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when the signature field is absent from the challenge payload, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker who strips the signature key from the challenge JSON passes the condition as false, bypassing tamper-detection entirely. The PoW solution check then runs against unverified parameters — allowing an attacker to…

item.title: Multiple Path Traversal vulnerabilities in CAST Imaging
item.description: CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files. Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL…

item.title: Outstatic: Authenticated GitHub REST proxy can send OAuth token to non-GitHub origins
item.description: Impact Outstatic’s authenticated GitHub REST proxy accepted an unvalidated endpoint parameter and constructed an upstream GitHub API URL by string concatenation while attaching the authenticated user’s GitHub OAuth token. A user with access to the Outstatic dashboard could craft a request that caused the server to send their own GitHub OAuth token to a non-GitHub host. If that token was captured, it could be used…

item.title: Path Traversal vulnerability in CAST Imaging
item.description: CAST Imaging is vulnerable to Path Traversal vulnerability in "/api/server-folders" and "/api/server-folders/download" endpoints. These file-management endpoints accept user-supplied filesystem paths and allow selected system commands to be executed at the specified location, but they do not enforce sufficient authorization boundaries or restrict access to a predefined set of resources. An authenticated attacker…

item.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated full-response SSRF in Atomic-Server /bookmark endpoint
item.description: Summary Atomic-Server exposes a GET /bookmark endpoint that fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side, parses the response, and reflects the fetched content back to the caller. The endpoint requires no authentication and performs no authorization of its own, and the underlying fetch helper applies no allow-list or private-IP deny-list. An unauthenticated attacker with network reach to the server can force it to…

item.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated /setup invite grants write access to the entire Drive
item.description: Summary atomic-server provisions a well-known invite at {server}/setup with write = true , target = the Drive root, and usagesLeft = 1 . Invite redemption ignores the redeemer's identity ( for agent: in server/src/plugins/invite.rs:22 ), so possession of the URL is the only requirement. An unauthenticated attacker who sends GET /setup?public-key= has the server create a new Agent and grant it write access to the…

item.title: Atomic Server: Arbitrary file read via user-controlled internalId in the /download handler (leaks root agent private key)
item.description: Summary The Commit apply path enforces no allowlist of writable properties , so any authenticated Agent can set the internalId string (datatype string , no character validation) on a resource it owns. item.title: Atomic Server: Stored XSS via uploaded files served inline (same-origin) on /download → account takeover
item.description: Summary Files uploaded via POST /upload are served back by GET /download/{path} using actix files::NamedFile . For text/html and image/svg+xml , actix-files (0.6.6) sets Content-Disposition: inline , so the browser renders the file instead of downloading it. item.title: Hardcoded Authentication Token in CAST Imaging
item.description: CAST Imaging contains a hardcoded authentication token in the "KeyCloakController" class of auth-service.jar. An attacker who gains access to the source code, application package, logs, or configuration files can reuse this token to call auth-service endpoints without authentication. An attacker with access to the web server process or with write access to the LMS database can register a malicious library and trigger a configuration reload, causing lmsd to load and execute it. item.title: Remote Code Execution in LMS

The mail parser does not reject Apache .htaccess configuration files or PHP-executable files when saving ticket attachments. A remote unauthenticated attacker can e-mail a Helpdesk ticket with such an attachment; in the default configuration, anyone can request the uploaded file's URL which executes…

item.title: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
item.description: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.
